by Sulayman Shahid Mufassir
 The Bible’s Preview
 of Muhammad
 Despite the disastrous human interference in the holy writings of the Torah
 and the Gospel, as admitted by the Bible’s publishers, the scriptures still
 contain a goodly portion of the original truth. So much so that those who
 truly believe and follow the Bible, even in its present form, will certainly
 be guided to Islam (Qur’an 2:121). Those who honestly follow the teachings
 of Moses and Jesus (may God bestow blessings and peace upon them), even
 in their current state, will be led to the completion and fulfillment of what
 their creator expects of them. This has been the experience of many free-
 minded followers of the Bible. One such example is the author of this article.
 As a former ordained Christian minister, Sulayman Shahid Mufassir re-
 counts the biblical guidance which led him to the light of Islam.
 Tur Bice contains a vivid preview of the person and mission of Muhammad
 (peace be upon him) that is so distinct and unmistakable that many a sincere
 Jew and Christian was happy to accept him as the prophet when he appeared.
 But over the subsequent centuries of theological antagonism, preceded and
 accompanied by the editing, rewriting and dogmatizing of portions of the
 scriptural record, that written portrait has become obscured as with a thick
 layer of dust. When the centuries-old encrustations of dogma and sectarian
 hermeneutics are removed, many well-known, little understood verses of the
 Bible serve as signposts for the serious scholar.
 The Role of the Bible
 Muslims believe that the original Torah and Gospel were revealed by
 Almighty God. When Jesus began to call the Jews to return to sincere and
 devoted service to God, the Torah of Moses had been subjected to serious
 instances of careless copying and dogmatic editing, but he confirmed in his
 preaching whatever remained intact of the divine revelation. He said, “Do
 _hot suppose that I have come to abolish the Law (Torah) and the prophets;
 Did not come to abolish, but to complete. I tell you this: so long as heaven
 _and earth endure, not a letter, not a stroke, will disappear from the Law

Sulayman Shahid Mufassir
 Double Honor due to Ishmael’s Line
 The writers of Genesis wrongly attempted to make it appear that Ishmael
 would receive an inferior blessing because his mother was a servant woman,
 put Isaac, being the son of the free woman, would inherit the glory of the
 first-born son. In so doing, they disregarded the clear family laws of the
 Torah. According to this law, the rights of the first-born son are not invalid
 due to the social status of his mother. This applied especially in polygamous
 ges such as that of Abraham(8). Man’s social prejudices do not in
 maria:
 any way dictate the favor of God. According to the Torah:
 ل‎ F239 Sor x? oe? ps
 “Jf a man has two wives, one loved and the other unloved (i.e., slighted‏
 or socially despised due to inferior social status), and both the loved and‏
 the unloved have borne him sons, but the first-born is the son of the unloved‏
 wife, when he wills his property to his sons, he may not treat as first-born‏
 the son of the loved one in disregard of the son of the unloved one who‏
 is older. Instead he must accept the first-born, the son of the unloved one,‏
 and allot him a double portion of all he possesses; since he is the first fruit‏
 of his vigor, the birthright is his due”(9).‏
 But the Bible disregards this fair principle and gives throughout the
 “double portion” of honor to Isaac, the second son and makes it actually
 appear that the “birthright” is his (Cf. Genesis 17:21: “but My covenant
 will I establish with Isaac, whom Sarah shall bear ...”). This makes the
 “Torah” of the Bible a contradictory law. By right, the double honor and the
 birthright belong to the line of Ishmael, and the “unloved” social status
 of his mother detracts from this not at all.
 Ishmael’s descendants came to be known as Arabs, a term which, in
 Hebrew, meant those who inhabited the ‘arab or desert (10). It is not a
 coincidence that of the twelve sons of Ishmael (Genesis 25:12-16) the one
 mentioned most prominently is Qaydar (Cedar in Hebrew). In some Bible
 verses, Qaydar is synonymous with the Arabs in general(11). This is an
 important indication that the line of Qaydar was marked by God for a unique
 purpose, to bring forth the one whose life and work would bring “a double
 portion” of honor to the house of Ishmael.
 The nature. of this twofold honor begins to be revealed in the Old
 Testament book of Isaiah. There are many brilliant parables and prophecies
 in Isaiah which concern the fulfillment of God’s promise to bless all mankind

 he could be called A/-Amin, or as the Greek text of John 16:13 says, 73 mveipa
 ris ddnBetas, “the spirit of truth,” one of whom it could be said: “He has
 brought them the Truth.” (Qur’an 23:70).
 The term “spirit” here does not mean that the coming prophet would
 be other than human. In New Testament Greek, this word has also been
 applied to an inspired person, “the possessor of a spiritual communication”
 or revelation. The one who becomes overwhelmed with a divine revelation
 is himself termed a “spirit”(20). The “spirit of truth” would be the person
 who would possess a spiritual communication, that is, a divine revelation,
 and whose life and conduct and character would be marked to an extreme
 degree by devotion to the truth. This is why the next sentence of the verse
 containing this expression says: “He will guide you unto all truth; for he
 shall not speak of himself, but whatsoever he shall hear (from God), that
 shall he speak.” (John 16:13). This person would receive the revelation of
 truth from God and these words alone would constitute the message, not
 his own opinions or the writings of his companions. His message or revelation
 would be first and foremost and literally the Word of God. Note that this
 corresponds exactly to what God revealed to Moses about the prophet who
 would come from among the “brothers” of the Hebrews: “I... will put
 My words in his mouth, and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command
 him.” (Deuteronomy 18:18).
 A more striking point is the similarity between the divine mission given
 to Moses, Jesus and the Spirit of Truth (Muhammad) as bearers of a single
 thread of Revelation from God. By comparing Deuteronomy 18:15, 17-19;
 John 12:49; 16:12-13; and Qur’an 73:15, one observes that despite the
 thousands of years involved and the disastrous human interference in the
 Bible, the words describing these three personalities are almost identical.
 Therefore, the (original) Torah, Gospel and the Qur’an have One Source
 and reveal the same Truth, which is Eternal.
 It cannot be overlooked that Jesus gives a unique requirement that would
 help to identify the last prophet: “He shall glorify me.” (John 16:14). If
 anyone had come claiming to be this prophet, but did not give due honor
 to Jesus as prophet and Messiah, he would be the wrong one. As a nation,
 the Jews rejected Jesus. At the same time, this prophet to come would not
 bea follower of Jesus, that is, a Christian, because Jesus said that this prophet
 would reveal things of which Jesus himself was unaware. If Jesus had brought
 “all the truth,” there would have been no need for him to single out someone
 else who would come with all the truth. Likewise, since this prophet would
 bring all the truth he would have to be the last one, the seal of the prophets.
 Therefore, we would have to look for someone who, like Abraham in whose
 line he would come, would be neither Jew nor Christian but would believe

 “ANOTHER OF THE SAME KIND.” The Greek word for “another of
 a different kind” is heteros, but the New Testament does not use this word
 at John 14: 16. Clearly, then, the Paraclete would be ‘ANOTHER OF THE
 _ SAME KIND” as Jesus, or as Moses said, “Like unto me”: a MAN, not
 a spirit:
 Detail of the Revelation
 We can now begin to put together the complete “picture” which emerges
 from the Bible and come up with a very specific, graphic portrait of the
 messenger whose prominent characteristics are twofold: (1) He would be
 the last one and (2) he would be universal. According to the information
 given in the Old and New Testaments, this prophet would:
 i. be firm but merciful
 ii. establish a community based on justice
 iii. be a light for all the nations
 iv. be associated with Qaydar;
 (All based on Isaiah 42:1-11)
 v. be a descendant of Ishmael, a “brother” to the Hebrews
 vi. fulfill the promises made to Abraham and Ishmael to
 a. serve as a blessing to all the nations
 b. establish the Arabs as a “great nation”
 c. inherit the “double portion” of honor;
 vii. receive revelation directly from God;
 (All based on Genesis 17:20; 22:16-18; Deuteronomy 21:15-17)
 viii. come after Jesus’ mission was ended
 ix. comfort and counsel mankind (paraclete), for which he would be
 known as the praised one (periclyte)
 x. be outstanding for his truthfulness
 xi. receive words directly from God
 xii. deliver “all the truth,” the whole truth
 xiii. have a ministry of lasting effect
 xiv. glorify Jesus.
 (All based on John 14:16, 17 and 16:13, 14)
 To refine these points for still clearer focus, the last prophet would differ
 from all the others in at least three vital aspects:
 (1) He would have a universal mission
 (2) He would be the seal of the prophets
 : (3) He would be an Arab, and of the 12 sons of Ishmael, he would
 have to come in the line of Qaydar.
 1394/1974, 1(1)

Pope Sheila III
 False Points of Disagreement
 Certain statements in the Qur’an are misunderstood by some people, creating
 thereby erroneous impressions about Christianity. Examples of these im-
 sessions include the notion that the Christians are polytheists, that they
 consider Mary divine, that they believe in a son of God in the “physical”
 sense, and that God had a wife.
 1. Divinity of the Virgin Mary: This erroneous impression was created in the
 minds of some people on the basis of verse 116 in sura Al-Ma-idah (No.
 5). This verse states,

 God will ask, “O Jesus, son of Mary, have you told the people to
 worship you and your mother instead of God?” He will answer, “Glory
 be to You. How could I tell them what was not right? Had I told
 them that, you would have known about it. For You know my secrets,
 while I know not Your Secrets. Surely, You are fully aware of all
 secrets.”
 Christianity does not believe in the divinity of Mary, and any impression
 to that effect is erroneous. In fact, Mary herself is reported in the Gospel
 as a “slave of the Lord.” (Luke 1:38) Thus, she placed herself with the
 slaves of God. Consequently, if any group resorts to the deification of
 Mary should be disowned, and even opposed by the Christians. Fur-
 therefore, Christianity would not advocate the worship of anyone else
 besides God, even if Christ is one of those other gods. Christians believe
 in one God, and I will discuss this point towards the end of the article.
 2. Did God take a “wife” unto Himself? The erroneous impression that some
 Christians believe that God took for Himself a wife resulted probably
 from the Qur’anic verse 101 of sura Al-An‘am (No. 6). This verse states,
 He is the originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have
 © son, when He never took unto Himself a wife?
 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(1)

Pope Sheniida III
 dignity. The concept of trinity is totally different. We Say in it, “In the
 name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, ONE God, Amen.”
 Therefore, God is one divine entity, and He has a mind, and a soul.
 The three are one. Just like fire; though it is one thing, heat and also
 light are generated therefrom. The fire, its heat, and its light constitute
 but one entity. Similarly, man and his mind and his soul constitute but
 one entity. As for the sonship part of the trinity, it is like the sonship of
 thought to the mind. The mind begets thought, yet it has no spouse.
 Finally, what we discussed in this article does not mean that the Qur’an
 and Christianity agree on all points. Certainly, there are points of dis-
 agreement, and fundamental doctrinal differences. These involve the trinity,
 the resurrection of Christ, salvation, the divinity of Christ, his crucifixion,
 >
 the esoteric teachings of the church, and the Qur’an itself. But we wished
 to limit this article to the points of agreement rather than the points of
 disagreement.
 : 27

by Yusuf Amin Wah, Ph.D.
 ISLAM:
 Was It Spread by the Sword?
 Far from being apologetic, this article states the facts, and addresses the
 question, “If Islam were spread by the sword, :
 how can we account for
 the fact that the Muslims in the ‘unconquered’
 lands vastly outnumber their
 brethren in the Arab world?” Professor Wali is
 a board member and treasurer
 of the Supreme Council of the Muslim You
 th Organization, Cairo, Egypt.
 A dominant impression upon the students of “Tslam,” “Comparative Religion,”
 _ or “Religions of the World,” in many academic institutions is all too often
 that “Islam was spread by the sword.” Whether this impression is the result
 of deliberate prejudice, or due to ignorance, the teachers who convey this
 distorted “truth” are doing a great disservice to themselves and their students.
 Ironically, those who rise to “defend” Islam have quite frequently fallen
 into a trap, inadvertently misrepresenting the truth about Islam themselves.
 In their zeal and enthusiasm, they often counter the various malicious remarks
 by those ignorant of Islam with emotional and apologetic articles which effect
 a devaluation of certain Islamic principles. Thus, they almost invariably
 overlook the important concept of jihad in Islam (striving in the cause of
 God). They tend to limit the scope of jihad, and apologize for every movement
 thereof that it was in “self-defense.”
 Since the time of the prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) many
 who opposed him and those who persist in opposing evident truth overlook
 the fundamental principles of religious belief in Islam. Thus, they overlook
 the basic Islamic principle that “there shall be no compulsion in religion
 Ab ” (Qur’an 2:256). Within the Islamic society, therefore, every
 individual must be guaranteed absolute freedom to belive in whatever he
 chooses. It is instructive to look at the heritage of Islam regarding this matter.
 Establishing and maintaining the Islamic system inside as well as outside
 the Arabian peninsula did make jihad inevitable under certain circumstances.
 The very first Islamic jihad outside Arabia illustrates this. During the sixth
 year of Hijra (Islamic calendar), the prophet Muhammad (peace be upon
 him) received the first divine command to preach Islam universally; that Islam
 ‘Was intended for all the people, all places, and all times. In obedience to
 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(1): 29-37 3

Yusuf Amin Wali
 «ll praise is due to God. I praise Him, seek His help, believe
 in Him, and trust in Him. I hereby bear witness that there is
 no deity except God; there is none who rivals Him. O children
 of ‘Abdul-Muttalib, O children of ‘Abd Manéf, © children of
 Zuhrah, O children of Tayyim, O children of Makhziim, O children
 of Asad, God has commanded me to preach His message to those
 around me. Let it be known that I can offer you no material gains
 of this world, nor can I help you in the hereafter. My sole function
 is to deliver the message to you, and ask you to believe that there
 is no god except the one God.”
 With this, a most important page in the history of mankind unfolded
 and the call of Islam began, characterized by tolerance, moderation, aad.
 a whole new set of moral ethics. From that moment on, the spread of Islam
 was effected mainly by the high moral character of the religion’s adherents.
 The people of Arabia, and later in other parts of the world, witnessed Islam
 through the behavior and the personal conduct of Muslims in their daily
 life. It was predominantly this example of personal conduct rather than the
 Qur’an alone that brought about the massive spread of Islam. The primary
 influence was by the Muslims themselves as they observed the Islamic way
 of life. Once this primary influence was manifested, the onlookers sought
 out the religion by approaching the Qur’an and the teachings of Muhammad
 (God’s blessings and peace be upon him): A well-known, well-documented,
 example of this process is the case of ‘Umar b. Al-Khattab.
 In his pagan days, ‘Umar was an ardent opponent of the new religion.
 One can imagine his fury when he learned that his own sister and her
 husband had adopted Islam. It was the behavior of this couple under ‘Umar’s
 severe beating that led to ‘Umar’s Islam. The patience, tolerance, and
 steadfastness of his sister and brother-in-law awakened him and aroused his
 curiosity. Thus, their Islamic conduct in the face of his relentless anger exerted
 the primary influence in the guidance process. He then asked about the
 religion, its principles, and the Qur'an. By the time they explained the religion
 to him, and after he heard portions of the Qur’an, he became convinced
 that Islam was the religion for him. This example illustrates three important
 points:
 1. It was the newly acquired character of ‘marks sister and her husband
 that aroused his interest in the religion.
 2. The qur'an influence came second to complete the guidance process.
 ‘Umar was overwhelmed by the common sense and beauty of the Qur’an.
 He ended up begging his victims to take him to Muhammad.
 3. Certainly, a powerful man like ‘Umar did not adopt Islam by force or
 under any kind of threat.
 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(1)

 The periods of war are governed by Islamic rules which are characterized
 py tolerance and moderation. Thus, pledges of security to the opposing
 warriors must be respected. Indeed Islam has transcended the limits of
 tolerance in regard to the question of security so much so that should a
 Muslim make a hostile sign to warn an enemy of the impending attack and
 the latter took it for a sign of peace, it is imperative that full security should
 be vouchsafed him in accordance with what he understood the sign to mean.
 Such is the rule in war-time. The security of the enemy who enters
 a Muslim country with the object of engaging in trade or business rests
 entirely in the hands of those in authority. Should a member of the public
 however give his pledge to an enemy who thereby gains admittance into
 the country for trade and the latter thinks such pledge is binding, full security
 should be accorded him and if the Wali (governor) does not deem it in
 the interest of the country that such security be given, he had to conduct
 the enemy back to safety.
 Again should an enemy ask for security in order to have an insight
 into religion and it happens that he finds no satisfaction in Islam, he is
 to be sent back in full security to his own abode of safety, as ordained by
 the following verse:

 Qur’an recited and acquaint himself with the truth thereof, grant him
 protection till he has heard it, then give him a safe conduct if he
 chooses not to profess Islam, to his abode of safety. (9:6)
 The pledge of security in Islam is a real one, no mere idle talk. It lays
 Particular stress on the safe custody of the wealth and property of those

 law of God to which we are created, there is no better law than His!

 These5 admitted
 by reason on mere contemplation for they are among its primary
 axioms. sae : .
 4 As to the source of religions being one in all times, no other fact could
 be more acceptable to reason, for truth is one and could never be more.
 As to religion being a divine institution identical with the natural in-
 stincts, it is a fact that admits of no doubt for souls are prone to seek the
 truth and submit to its judgment so long as they are guided by the light
 of pure reason.
 As to the tendency to iniquity, disregard of reason and blind imitation
 of the practices of ancestors being the cause of differences which divide people
 among themselves, it is a fact that no one could gainsay and is well borne
 t by history.
 Should man rid himself of all these imperfections and appeal to reason

 The Invocations of
 ‘Abdullah Ansari : 1
 ‘4abdullah Ansari, a famous Persian Sufi, was born in Herat 396 AH (1005
 C.E.). It is said that one of his ancestors was a companion of the prophet
 Muhammad (God’s blessings and peace be upon him) who moved to Herat
 with Asap, son of Qays. Ansari’s father, Abu Manner Muhammad Ansari,
 became a permanent resident of Herat.
 These invocations, translated into English by Sir Jogendra Singh, contain
 true advice to guide the Pilgrim along the path of discipleship to the temple
 of peace. They come from a man who himself had trodden the path and
 found what his heart desired.
 When ‘Abdullah Ansari departed from this world, he was 85 years old,
 leaving behind a wealth of Sufi knowledge. Among his well-known works
 are Risala Munajat (The Book of Prayer), Tabagat-ul-Siifiyyah (The
 Book of Sufis), Zad-ul-‘Arifin (Provisions of the Sufi Teachers), and
 Kitab-i-Israr (The Book of Mysteries).
 In the name of God,
 Most Gracious,
 Most Merciful.
 O Thou Munificent One
 Who art the bestower
 Of all bounties,
 O Thou wise One
 Who overlooked our faults,
 O Self-existent One
 Who art beyond our comprehension,
 O Thou omnipotent One
 Who hast no equal in power and greatness,
 Who art without a second:
 O Thou merciful One
 LAM 1394/1974, 1(1): 67-69 1

 Over the first five issues of ISLAM, the Journal will publish this table
 for convenient conversion of dates from either of the two calendar systems.
 Such chronological conversion tables have been difficult to find yet most
 indispensible for the Western scholar of Islam. Since all great works of
 Islamic literature refer exclusively to Hijra dates, the Editors feel that these
 tables will be useful to many readers.

 be upon him) arrived at Medina on the 12th day of Rabi‘ I, coincident
 with September 24, 622 CE (Christian Era). This sets the first day of
 _ the first Hijra year (Muharram 1, 1) as July 16, 622. Fifteen hundred
 Hijra years will be covered in these tables (622-2076 CE).
